text:
ops-bot: ALERT -> paging oncall: high error rate from /v1/generate in us-east-1, auto-threshold triggered (5xx spike). paging: @Maya oncall (primary)
Maya: seeing 500s and some 502s. console metrics look normal for control-plane health but API error rate is high. starting live triage. @Sanjeev can you pull dataplane logs?
Sanjeev: on it. I see a cluster of backend failures from 1781005400-1781005480. Errors look like downstream handshake failures to the KV cache: "connection reset by peer" in logs. grabbing full stack now.
Eli: quick check — any deploys in the last 15m? deploy-bot: deploy 2026-02-20T14:01Z to inference-runtime succeeded on canary, rollout paused. No full rollout started. Nothing to account for broad failures.
Claire: customer page shows increased error rates for a handful of orgs in us-east-1, roughly 3% of requests returning 5xx. CS-Frank is on call for customer comms.
CS-Frank: ping — which customers affected? I'm ready to notify with ETA for mitigation.
Maya: list incoming — orgs: acme-inc, novella-ai, archive-saas. severity: degraded (not complete outage). include note: model responses failing intermittently. Do not escalate to customers yet until mitigation attempt.
Sanjeev: pasting log excerpt:
```
[1781005422] worker-12 ERROR handshake.go:91: kvcache handshake failed: EOF
[1781005423] worker-12 WARN retrying kvcache connect (attempt 1)
[1781005426] worker-12 ERROR api-handler.go:204: write response failed: broken pipe
```
Sanjeev: hypothesis 1: kvcache process crashed / restarted causing transient connection resets. hypothesis 2: control-plane config push contained a bad flag for kvcache timeouts (too low) causing premature disconnects.
Eli: note — console shows control-plane reconciliation success at 1781005410 for feature flag `kv.timeout-ms=30`. That's suspiciously low. Console UI shows the flag applied; dataplane agents report older value still served until full propagation.
Claire: so discrepancy: control-plane believes config pushed, console shows success, but dataplane still operating on old config OR in inconsistent state. that could explain 502s when timeout truncates connections.
Maya: mitigation options: A) increase kv.timeout-ms to safe default (200) and push to canary then broad. B) force restart kvcache on affected nodes. C) route traffic to fallback cluster. I propose option A + temporary rate-limit for affected orgs while we roll.
Sanjeev: can increase flag but worried about propagation lag. I can trigger a config-sync job to push immediately to dataplane agents. initiating: `bin/controlctl push-flag --key kv.timeout-ms --value 200 --env us-east-1` — running now.
ops-bot: ACTION -> config-push initiated by Sanjeev at 1781005490. Watch for `config-sync` events.
Sanjeev: config-sync logs show start ->
```
[1781005491] control: pushing flag kv.timeout-ms=200 to region us-east-1
[1781005492] control: ack from dataplane-agent 10.3.5.12: success
[1781005493] control: ack from dataplane-agent 10.3.5.13: success
[1781005498] control: ack from dataplane-agent 10.3.5.14: success
```
Eli: looks like a subset of agents acked quickly. are there any agents still missing? Sanjeev?
Sanjeev: one agent 10.3.5.15 shows `timeout waiting for handshake`. digging into that host.
Maya: while Sanjeev investigates node 5, I'll start a canary re-route for the 3 affected orgs to fallback cluster using `route override` for 30m. This reduces risk while we confirm.
Claire: CS-Frank prepping message: "We are investigating intermittent 5xx responses for a small subset of requests in us-east-1. We have a mitigation in progress and will update in 30 mins." Will send after you confirm canary route in place, Maya.
Maya: canary route applied at 1781005530. ops-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE -> traffic for acme-inc, novella-ai, archive-saas routed to fallback-cluster-02.
ops-bot: METRIC -> error rate for those orgs dropped from 3% -> 0.2% after route change (chart window 1781005520-1781005560).
Sanjeev: node 10.3.5.15 had old control-agent (v1.8.2) that didn't auto-apply new protocol for config ACKs — it's refusing config push. upgrading agent now.
Sanjeev: upgrade command: `apt-get install control-agent=1.9.0` -> completed at 1781005602. Re-running config push for that agent -> ack at 1781005610.
Eli: after full ack, kvcache timeouts are now 200ms across agents. I'm seeing decreased `broken pipe` errors in logs.
Sanjeev: logs post-fix:
```
[1781005612] worker-12 INFO handshake.go: handshake succeeded
[1781005615] worker-12 INFO api-handler.go: request completed status=200 duration=120ms
```
Maya: mitigation successful. rolling back the temporary route in 10 minutes if stable. final impact: ~3 customer orgs with intermittent errors for ~12 minutes. No data corruption.
CS-Frank: sending update to customers now: "Mitigation applied, service restored for affected requests. We will follow up with RCA and timeline." Will keep PS informed.
Eli: RCA notes to capture in-thread:
- Timeline: control-plane flag push at 1781005410 set `kv.timeout-ms=30` (too aggressive).
- Propagation: most dataplane agents updated, but one old agent (10.3.5.15) did not apply due to old control-agent binary.
- Failure mode: partial propagation created mixed config state -> some connections hit the lower timeout -> handshake failures and 5xx.
- Root cause: lack of agent version gating for config protocol changes + insufficient pre-check on flag value extremes.
Maya: Hypotheses tracked (label them H1,H2,H3):
H1: control-plane pushed low timeout (confirmed) -> increases 5xx (evidence: timing and logs) [Status: Confirmed]
H2: dataplane agent version mismatch caused partial propagation (evidence: agent 10.3.5.15 old binary) [Status: Confirmed]
H3: rollout tooling didn't block dangerous flag values (the console allowed 30ms) [Status: Likely]
Claire: next-actions for postmortem:
- create incident doc and timeline (owner: Maya)
- require deploy-blocker rule: control-plane should reject timeouts <50ms for kvcache unless explicit override (owner: Eli)
- add agent-version pre-check to config-push (owner: Sanjeev)
- notify infra to schedule a sweep to upgrade legacy agents (owner: Sanjeev)
- CS follow-up comms and affected customer list (owner: CS-Frank)
Maya: oncall handoff: I'm handing to Sanjeev for postmortem ops and follow-ups. Sanjeev, take it from here. Handoff at 1781005780.
Sanjeev: taking over. I'll open the incident doc and link logs. Creating postmortem draft and adding timeline + commands used. Also scheduling quick runbook update.
Maya: thanks — closing paging. ops-bot: CLOSE -> incident quiet, status: mitigated at 1781005821. Please file postmortem and link to this thread.
ops-bot: INCIDENT -> ticket INC-2026-2267 created and linked.
Claire: noted. tagging for follow-up meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll add attendees.
Eli: attaching quick log bundle path: s3://redwood-logs/1781005432/diag.tar.gz (contains full agent logs + control push traces) — keep for RCA.
Maya: final note for runbook: call out control-vs-dataplane discrepancy pattern and add a checklist for immediate routing to fallback cluster for partial propagation events. thanks team. :thumbsup:
